title: Cross-Mechanism Language Encoding Graph Atlas

nodes.label: Semantic Value Support
nodes.function_role: Forms candidate value support from object/category/relation/value conditions.

model_evidence.summary: Value support can be restored into several task contexts but does not guarantee generation.

nodes.sufficiency: Restore and protocol patches can raise correct-prefix rank and sometimes exact generation.
nodes.necessity: Necessary path not fully isolated; support alone is insufficient.
hard_limits: semantic support is mixed with protocol and readout policy
not yet a clean natural writer map
next_tests: separate same-value wrong-format and different-value same-format controls

nodes.label: Task Intent Gate
nodes.function_role: Permits or suppresses short-value behavior according to instruction/task demand.

model_evidence.summary: Value-to-task and task-to-value patches show task intent modulates short-answer protocol.

nodes.sufficiency: Value-to-task restore can pull non-value prompts toward value answers.
nodes.necessity: Task-to-value suppression shows intent can block short-answer support, but necessity is position dependent.
hard_limits: rank shifts often stronger than exact generation shifts
position effects are broad
next_tests: build pure intent controls without relation/content changes

nodes.label: Protocol Execution Field
nodes.function_role: Boundary and label-driven format/protocol trajectory controlling short answer vs explanation/newline behavior.

model_evidence.summary: Separator, label_aligned, relation_tail, and L17-L20/L20-L22 trajectories repeatedly control protocol.

nodes.sufficiency: Protocol trajectory restores can flip newline/explanation vs short-value generation in several models.
nodes.necessity: Necessary intervals exist, but side effects and model-specific boundaries remain.
hard_limits: protocol and semantic value are mixed at relation_tail/label sites
template sensitivity remains
next_tests: map protocol nodes across JSON/code/natural explanation formats

nodes.label: First Token Readout Closure
nodes.function_role: Makes correct answer prefix become top1 at the first generated token.

model_evidence.summary: Readout closure can be engineered, but Phase 665 shows it does not close full answer generation.

nodes.sufficiency: Readout/last-writer combinations can make correct_prefix top1.
nodes.necessity: Not sufficient for exact answer sequence.
hard_limits: projection norm and hidden direction are separable
first-token closure can still fail continuation
next_tests: record multi-competitor margins for every future generation test

nodes.label: Multi-Competitor Readout

model_evidence.summary: Top1 replacement and pairwise margins are insufficient; multi-competitor view better explains failure.

nodes.sufficiency: Multi-competitor correction identifies hidden blockers missed by pairwise tests.
hard_limits: competitor sets must be updated for each task format
next_tests: extend competitor taxonomy beyond ORV values to JSON/code/explanation tasks

nodes.label: Format Continuation State
nodes.function_role: General continuation state after correct_prefix that keeps generation in a format/protocol route.
nodes.sufficiency: Correct and mismatch restores can both repair some early boundaries, showing general continuation state.
nodes.necessity: Zero removal can be destructive but not semantically specific.
hard_limits: mismatch_restore is not a pure semantic control
format state and value state are entangled

nodes.label: Value-Specific Token1 Transition State
nodes.function_role: Controls transition from answer-entry token to first content-discriminative value token.
nodes.sufficiency: Correct_restore beats mismatch_restore on key boundaries, especially DS7B and qwen3 L23/L22 boundary.
nodes.necessity: Zero_remove often destroys token1, but this also affects scale/format/position.
hard_limits: small sample counts: qwen3=5, glm4=4, ds7b=12
not generalized beyond ORV short values yet

nodes.label: Writer Topology
nodes.function_role: Mechanism topology that writes value-specific token1 transition state.
nodes.sufficiency: qwen3 head10+head11 ensemble shows strong semantic subchannel; DS7B requires full boundary state.
nodes.necessity: Single-head closure rejected as a universal explanation.
hard_limits: o_proj head slice is not full Q/K/V causal path
layernorm/residual scale untested
next_tests: test layernorm and residual scale controls
Q/K/V pattern decomposition only on confirmed ensemble candidates

nodes.label: Residual Boundary Integrated State
nodes.function_role: Integrated residual state at layer_out/layer_input boundaries that cannot be reduced to small writer sets.
nodes.sufficiency: DS7B full L21 layer_out / L22 layer_input restores token1 strongly and specifically.
nodes.necessity: Small head/component ensembles fail to close DS7B.
hard_limits: may include normalization/scale state not captured by component restores
next_tests: directly decompose layernorm input/output and residual scale

nodes.label: Continuation Controller
nodes.function_role: Stabilizes answer sequence after entry token; Phase 665 shows early token1 bottleneck dominates current failures.
nodes.sufficiency: If token1 is forced correct, token2 is usually top1 in selected failures.
nodes.necessity: Later continuation beyond token2 is not yet fully audited.
hard_limits: current exact generation tests use short values and small failure sets
next_tests: extend forced continuation audit to token3+ and longer answer formats

edges.note: Intent can permit or suppress the value support route.
Intent and protocol jointly choose short answer vs explanation/full sentence behavior.
Protocol trajectory can make correct prefix accessible to first-token readout.
Correct prefix must beat multiple policy competitors.
Top1 prefix does not guarantee continuation route; format continuation state is separate.
Phase 666 separates general continuation from value-specific token1 transition.
Writer topology is model-specific; qwen3 small head ensemble, DS7B residual boundary.
Full residual boundaries can dominate small writer ensembles.
Once token1 is correct, token2 tends to stabilize in current failures.

global_findings: The token1 transition gate local phase is complete enough to stop single-head chasing.
The current atlas has stable functional nodes but model-specific implementation topology.
The largest open gap is not another local patch, but clean graph-scale controls and purer semantic/format counterfactuals.
hard_limits: Several nodes are based on ORV short-value tasks and require format/generalization tests.
Mismatch restore is useful but not a pure semantic intervention.
Zero removal proves necessity only in a broad state-distribution sense.
Natural writer paths are still partly unresolved because head-slice tests do not decompose Q/K/V and attention pattern.

next_phase.title: Graph Atlas Counterfactual Control Set
next_phase.goal: Build clean same-value/different-format and different-value/same-format counterfactuals for the atlas nodes before running new model tests.
next_phase.reason: The atlas shows the main bottleneck is control purity, not absence of local candidates.
